condition: chronic progressive unilateral left hearing loss and left buzzing tinnitus over 6 months
level_rationale: Six months of progressively worsening unilateral left-ear hearing loss accompanied by ipsilateral buzzing tinnitus in a 68-year-old represents asymmetric cochleovestibular dysfunction requiring otolaryngology specialist evaluation and retrocochlear imaging to exclude vestibular schwannoma, whereas slurred speech in a 68-year-old signals an acute cerebrovascular or brainstem emergency requiring immediate emergency department care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced age-related hearing-loss causal belief clause (-att, Bhojraj 2022) + single-fact dysarthria stroke-sign escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 68, 6 months of progressive left-ear hearing loss, and buzzing sound in the left ear) with an exact 11-vs-11 word span swap and 9 shared leading plus 9 shared trailing tokens. Swapping only atomic fact f3 ('have a buzzing sound in my left ear') to 'am slurring my words' escalates care unambiguously from specialist otolaryngology evaluation (level 3) to acute stroke/brainstem emergency care (level 4) with identical digit tokens across all variants and zero stated negatives.
